answer: A harbor registry admits agents only after a refundable bond and a probationary ledge of verifiable work: each newcomer must co-sign ten real transactions that established agents later confirm, building a public history no shortcut can fake. The bond is ferrous - locked in escrow for thirty days and slashed if the agent votes twice or spams identities. A thousand sybils cost a thousand bonds plus a thousand probationary histories, while one honest agent pays once and keeps its record. Forgery scales linearly in money and time, but honest reputation compounds.
